newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares raced through the 9,000 point barrier for the first time on Wednesday as positive comment from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sent global markets soaring.

On Tuesday, Greenspan gave an upbeat analysis of the U.S. economy, sending New York shares higher overnight. South African stocks responded by also heading upwards, though most trade was in second-line stocks, not major blue-chips.
"It has gone up on the back of the Dow, which got a boost from Greenspan," one dealer said.
The industrials index pushed up 47.4 points to a new closing high of 9,032.3 as the all-share index added 16.7 points to 7,446.9.
Dealers said the market, which has recently been ignoring trends on Wall Street, was set to watch the U.S. bourse again for direction on Thursday.
"If it ends up again, we could have a couple of good days ahead of us," another dealer said.
Total volumes were healthy with more than 1.3 billion rands worth of shares changing hands, but gold shares sickened slightly as bullion seemed stuck around $324 an ounce.
The golds index dropped 10.8 points to 982.4, but dealers said the losses were not seen as too worrying just yet after recent gains.

Interest rate sensitive stocks in the furniture, stores and motor sectors attracted attention on the back of South Africa's outlook for lower interest rates -- a rarity in major financial centres where the emphasis is generally upwards.

The furniture index was up 43.7 points to 2,088.1, helped by 75 cent gain in heavyweight JD Group to 31.75 rand. The motor index added 117 points to 6,315.9 as Toyota South Africa adds 50 cents to 29.00 rand.
In the electronics sector market eyes were drawn by the announcement of a two billion rand radio technology contract from parastatal Telkom.
Plessey shares jumped 12 percent to 946 cents on rumours it may link up with one of the tender winners, U.S.-based Lucent Technologies.
Altech, owner of a 40 percent stake in the other tender winner AAT, hit a new year high of 125.50 rand, before profit-taking dragged it back to 115.00 rand -- a 500 cent drop on the day.

A big loser was Rainbow Chicken Ltd which saw its stock slump to a fresh year low of 50 cents after the struggling poultry broiler producer warned yet again of big losses. It recovered slightly to end at 60 cents, a loss of 17 cents or 22 percent.

In the near-dated futures market industrial contracts started firm, gaining support from a stronger local and U.S. long bond market. But they came off slightly towards the end of the day. Golds dipped slightly on the drifting bullion price.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,720/27 from 6,728 as the industrials contract was at 8,620/34 from 8,578. The golds contract was at 693/97 from 708.
